h1: Garage Building in Rocky View County
heroSub: Springbank, Bearspaw, Langdon and the Balzac area: bigger lots, bigger garages and shops, and a different permit authority from the City of Calgary. Get two or three written quotes before the spring rush.
introHtml:
Garage building in Rocky View County is a different job from a garage off a Calgary back lane. The County wraps Calgary, with acreages in areas such as Springbank, Bearspaw, Langdon and the Balzac area, and lots there often have room for a double, a triple or a shop. Back Lane Garage Co is an advertising site that puts you in touch with independent garage builders. It does not build, hold a licence or pull permits itself.

Your permit authority is Rocky View County, not the City of Calgary, so the City's rules and fee schedule do not apply to your project. Get two or three comparable written quotes early, ideally over winter, and confirm every permit question with the County before you sign. Call (403) 555-0162 to get started.

sections.heading: Permits: Rocky View County, not the City
sections.html:
Rocky View County says building permits are required for demolition or construction of any building over 107 square feet (10 m²). Its development permit page lists garages among the projects that do not need a development permit if they comply with the Land Use Bylaw. Whether yours complies depends on your land use district, so ask the County rather than assuming.

This page does not quote size, height or setback limits, because they vary by district. Do not borrow Calgary's numbers or a neighbouring town's. If your property is inside a town, a different permit authority applies: see Airdrie, Cochrane, Okotoks or Chestermere.

The County's 2026 Master Rates Bylaw sets building permit fees per square foot: $0.30 for an unfinished residential garage under 592 sq ft (55 m²), $0.40 over that size and $0.58 for a finished one, plus a 4% Safety Codes levy. On that published rate, an unfinished 24 by 24 garage (576 sq ft) works out to $172.80 before the levy. Confirm the current rate and how it applies to your design with the County.

sections.heading: Trusses, slabs and hail on a bigger build
sections.html:
Rocky View County says the provincial truss standard, STANDATA 23-BCI-015R1, applies to all Part 9 buildings from 1 March 2026. Its September 2026 accessory building checklist says all truss profiles and layouts must be stamped by a licensed Alberta engineer. Wide spans and tall walls mean bigger trusses, so ask each builder whether stamped truss drawings are in the quote.

For foundations, the County offers pre-engineered slab-on-grade designs for eligible single-storey detached residential garages. A garage with a second floor or mezzanine needs a site-specific engineered foundation design, according to the same checklist. If you are planning loft storage, tell every builder up front, and see the page on custom garages.

Hail is worth pricing in. The June 2020 storm that hit Calgary, Airdrie, Rocky View County and the surrounding area caused almost $1.2 billion in insured damage, according to CatIQ as reported by the Insurance Bureau of Canada. One Calgary builder, Corsac Construction, offers James Hardie siding for its durability against Calgary's weather, including hail. Ask each builder what roofing and siding is included.

sections.heading: What bigger garages cost and how to compare quotes
sections.html:
The prices below are what Calgary builders advertise on their own sites, not quotes from this page, and none of them is specific to Rocky View County. Corsac Construction advertises a large double (24' x 24') from $29,900 plus GST and a triple (36' x 20') from $49,000 plus GST. For taller and wider builds, the PCND cost guide puts oversized, triple or tall-door garages (26 feet wide or more, or extra ceiling height) at $90,000 to $140,000+, and calls those typical market ranges rather than fixed prices. See the Calgary garage cost page for more.

Heat and insulation change the price. PCND says insulating and drywalling a double adds roughly $6,000 to $15,000, and a forced-air or radiant tube heater adds $2,500 to $6,000. Start from garage packages if you want a baseline, then add what your acreage build needs.

Ask each builder to price the same size, door height, electrical service, heat and truss package, and to say who applies for the permits. If a builder wants money before the work is done, Service Alberta's licence search lists Prepaid Contractor licences, and a licence is not an endorsement of quality. Get the quote itemized and in writing.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a garage in Rocky View County?
faq.a: The County says building permits are required for construction of any building over 107 square feet (10 m²). Its development permit page says garages do not need a development permit if they comply with the Land Use Bylaw, and compliance depends on your district. Confirm with Rocky View County before any work starts.

faq.q: Do Calgary's garage rules apply on my acreage?
faq.a: No. Rocky View County is a separate municipality with its own permit authority, fee bylaw and Land Use Bylaw. Calgary's size, height and setback numbers do not carry over, and this site does not quote County limits because they vary by district. Ask the County what applies to your land.

faq.q: What does a Rocky View County garage building permit cost?
faq.a: The County's 2026 Master Rates Bylaw lists $0.30 per square foot for unfinished residential garages under 592 sq ft, $0.40 per square foot over that size and $0.58 for finished ones, plus a 4% Safety Codes levy. That is the permit fee only, not a builder's price. Confirm the current rate with the County.

faq.q: Do roof trusses need an engineer's stamp in Rocky View County?
faq.a: The County's September 2026 checklist says all truss profiles and layouts must be stamped by a licensed Alberta engineer, and the provincial truss standard applies to Part 9 buildings from 1 March 2026. Ask each builder whether stamped truss drawings are in the quote, and confirm the requirement with the County.
